title: Affine compactness of the locally invertible open
statement: Let $W$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $M,N$ be finite locally free $\mathcal O_W$-modules with varying ranks [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf], and let $\varphi:M\to N$. Let $U_\varphi$ be its locally invertible open [def-sc-module-map-iso-locus]. For every affine open $V\subseteq W$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], the subset $V\cap U_\varphi$ of $W$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Final determinant sentence; Tag 05GD, Lemma 10.79.4(3), local matrix proof

proof.text: On the affine open V, refine simultaneous finite free frames of M and N to principal affine opens. Compactness of V selects finitely many frames covering V.

On an equal-rank frame the neighbourhood-defined locus is the determinant principal open: the adjugate supplies an inverse there, and invertibility at a stalk forces the determinant to be a unit. On unequal-rank frames the locus is empty by residue-field dimensions. Zero rank has determinant 1. These statements identify the intersection with the union defining U_phi.
The determinant principal opens in the finitely many affine frames are affine and compact; their images in V and W remain compact. Their finite union is V intersect U_phi.
